title: Least squares three ways
brief: Solve the same problem through the normal equations, QR, and the SVD, then watch the first one lose its digits.
hints: numpy.linalg.cholesky returns the lower factor L with A = L L^T. Solve L z = b, then L^T w = z, with scipy-free triangular solves built from numpy.linalg.solve_triangular's absence in mind: numpy has no triangular solve, so use scipy.linalg.solve_triangular.
numpy.linalg.qr(X, mode='reduced') gives the thin factorisation. R is upper triangular, so back substitution is a triangular solve against Q.T @ y.
For the pseudoinverse, zero out every singular value at or below rcond * s.max(), and invert only the rest. Slicing V and U to the surviving columns gives the minimum-norm solution for free.
condition_number is s.max() / s.min() from numpy.linalg.svd(X, compute_uv=False).
